scope: All checks below judge NETPLAY-scenario captures: a two-player lockstep session rendered from seat 1's view. Frames are either (a) full-screen session states (near-black screen with large centered text), (b) live world frames with netplay overlay text, or (c) live world frames under the semi-transparent MENU panel (J6-C: side panels LINK and SESSION flank the menu). The local player's body carries the familiar WHITE ring; the PARTNER's body carries a CYAN/teal ring and is otherwise dimmed like an ally. The three netplay scripts stage mutually exclusive endings (desync, connection lost, partner-left-after-quit), so any check whose beat is absent from this reel passes with why='not exercised by this script'. no_render_garbage always applies in full.

checks.check: At least one frame is a full-screen near-black state reading HOSTING - WAITING FOR PARTNER with a PORT number line beneath it, with no world visible behind. If the reel never shows a hosting frame, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.
At least one frame is a full-screen near-black state reading CONNECTING..., no world behind it. If absent, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.

In frames showing two living ringed pack bodies, exactly one carries the white ring and exactly one carries a clearly different cyan/teal ring - two pilots read at a glance, never two white rings. If no frame shows both ringed bodies alive, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.

Across the mid-run frames the white-ringed body and the cyan-ringed body occupy visibly different positions over time - both pilots are moving independently, not statues. If fewer than two frames show both rings, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.
When the LINK SLOW banner is present it is legible top-center and does not collide with or overlap the zone banner above it. If no frame shows LINK SLOW, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.

At least one frame shows WAITING FOR PARTNER followed by a millisecond count at the top-center over a live world frame - the game visibly waiting, not crashed. If absent, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.
When WAITING AT GATE is shown, a ringed body is standing on or beside the gold gate tile at the map edge and the cue text is legible. If absent, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.

When NO BODY - WAITING is shown, no white-ringed body is alive in the frame (the cyan-ringed partner may live on) and the bottom controls strip is absent. If absent, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.

When the desync ending is present: a full-screen darkened state reading DESYNC AT TICK <number> - SESSION ENDED with a smaller file path line beneath it; the frozen world may ghost through the veil. If this reel has no desync frames, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.

When the connection-lost ending is present: a full-screen darkened state reading CONNECTION LOST - SESSION ENDED, same delivery as the desync screen. If absent, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.

Every netplay overlay line that appears (hosting, connecting, stall, link slow, gate wait, no body, endings) is legible: readable contrast against what is behind it, not clipped at screen edges, not overlapped into gibberish by other UI. While the MENU panel is open its veil legitimately dims overlay cues behind it - judge cue legibility on menu-less frames.

When the quit ending is present: after the session ends the frame is a full-screen darkened state reading PARTNER LEFT - SESSION ENDED, same delivery as the desync/connection-lost screens (the frozen world may ghost through the veil) - the abandoned seat is TOLD why its world stopped, never left frozen-silent. No menu panel or other UI overlaps the ending text (a session end force-closes an open menu). If this reel has no post-quit frames, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.

Where the MENU panel is open over a live netplay world: two side panels flank it - a LINK-titled panel (rows naming SEAT, TICKS, D, STALLS, DESYNCS) and a SESSION-titled panel (a LEVEL row and a RUN timer row) - each row legible, and the netplay world still readable behind the veil. Across two menu-open frames the world or the TICKS row visibly advances (lockstep keeps flowing under an open menu). If no frame shows the menu open over a netplay world, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.

In mid-run world frames where a white-ringed body is alive, the three HP bars (top-left) and the bottom controls strip render normally - the netplay overlays add text but never break or displace the base UI. (While NO BODY - WAITING shows, the strip is absent BY DESIGN - do not judge those frames here.) If the reel has no qualifying frames, pass with why='not exercised by this script'.
No frame shows tearing, missing map, entities outside walls, or obviously corrupted output.
